clue.text: Equal in courage: 'to some players, particularly forward

parts.note: someone equal in courage to another is 'as bold as' them
the brass is the section of an orchestra playing trumpets, horns and trombones

explanation.surface: A team's attackers are told they match the rest for bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests footballers, with 'forward' a position on the pitch; here 'forward' means cheeky, and the players are orchestral musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone impudently confident, which is what forward means when said of a person's manner.

clue.text: A proper student, according to Pope

definitions.text: A proper student, according to Pope

parts.words: A proper student, according to Pope
parts.note: Alexander Pope wrote 'The proper study of mankind is man', so the proper student is one whose subject is humankind

explanation.surface: A well-behaved pupil earns the approval of the pontiff.
explanation.walkthrough: Pope is the poet Alexander Pope, not the head of the Catholic Church: his Essay on Man says 'The proper study of mankind is man'.
explanation.definitionFit: This scholar studies humankind, exactly the study the poet's famous line calls proper.

clue.text: Report about hard drug

indicators.note: about says the word for a report goes round the letter for hard

parts.note: a report is the bang of a gun
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A news story concerning an addictive narcotic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts H inside BANG. The report is a loud noise, not a written account.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an Indian preparation of cannabis leaves, an example of a narcotic.

clue.text: Cut off from main source of love and shut up

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, so its opening letter is taken

parts.note: taken as written
something shut up is locked away

explanation.surface: Someone is kept from their chief supply of affection and imprisoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of' takes the L of love. The 'main' is the sea, not the principal thing, so the definition runs three words further than it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic word for the open sea, and such a country has no coastline.

clue.text: Liar. I found tucking into, fruit

indicators.note: tucking into means eating one's way inside, so the letter sits within the fruit

parts.note: ananas is another name for the pineapple

explanation.surface: A fibber is caught helping himself to the fruit bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found tucking into' puts I inside ANANAS. In the Acts of the Apostles he was struck dead for lying to Peter.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical figure who lied about his gift became a byword for any teller of untruths.

clue.text: Sort of farce that could dispel. boredom?

indicators.note: to dispel is to scatter, so the letters of the next word are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A slapstick comedy good enough to cure tedium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that could dispel' is the anagram signal for BOREDOM. This kind of farce is a British stage comedy of mistaken identities and slamming doors.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a genre of stage comedy built on romantic mix-ups, so it is one type of the theatrical form.

clue.text: Highly placed characters in front of queue, say

wordplay.reading: A to the letter before Q

parts.words: characters in front of queue, say
parts.note: queue said out loud is the seventeenth letter, and the characters ahead of it in the alphabet run from the first letter 'to' the sixteenth

explanation.surface: Important people get to stand at the head of the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns queue into the letter Q; the characters before it in the alphabet are the range from A to P, written as three words.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something on the summit of a thing sits at its highest point.

clue.text: E.g. Oscar and Parisian caught in the act

indicators.note: something caught in another is held inside it

parts.note: an act of parliament is a statute
et is the French word for and

explanation.surface: A man called Oscar and a Frenchman are found red-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar is the Academy Award figurine, not a person, and 'caught in the act' hides the container signal 'caught in' and a law.
explanation.definitionFit: The film award is a small gilded figure, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Gun shooting Falstaff's sidekick

parts.note: to shoot is to start or dart suddenly, so shooting is starting
Pistol is Falstaff's swaggering companion in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 2 and Henry V

explanation.surface: A firearm goes off and hits the fat knight's companion.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the firearm fired to begin a race, an example of the weapon.

clue.text: Militiamen taking aim in front of range

indicators.note: in front of says the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: to train a gun on something is to aim it
a band is a range, as in an age or price band

explanation.surface: Part-time soldiers level their weapons before the firing ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in front of' gives the order. These were the citizen companies of 16th and 17th century England.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the trained companies of citizen soldiers in Stuart England, a historical example of a militia.

clue.text: Modern paintings, in old section?

parts.note: a section of something is a part

explanation.surface: Contemporary canvases hang oddly in a gallery's historic wing.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the 1960s abstract movement built on optical illusion, an example of recent painting.

clue.text: Star gets runs, .leading one cricket side's comeback

indicators.note: leading says this letter goes ahead of everything else

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the side's name is read from its end

parts.note: the leg side is the half of a cricket field behind the batter's legs

explanation.surface: The best batter scores, spearheading a team's recovery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading' puts R first; 'comeback' turns LEG into GEL. Leg is one half of a cricket field, not a team.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the brightest sun in the constellation Orion, so an example of a heavenly body.

clue.text: Confession of one who 'does religious work

definitions.meaning: to do someone is to swindle them, and a swindler owning up would say the first-person pronoun followed by a three-letter verb for cheat
a sacred painting of Christ or a saint, venerated in the Orthodox church

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is a cheat's admission, and as one it is a devotional painting.

clue.text: Indication queen is pleased by pronouncement

indicators.note: a pronouncement is something spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: per means by, as in per post

explanation.surface: A royal statement shows Her Majesty is happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronouncement' signals the sound of PER. The queen is an adult female cat, not a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen is a female cat, and this rumbling noise is how a cat shows contentment.

clue.text: Unpleasant private Joe ordered about

indicators.note: ordered about means pushed around, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A nasty soldier is bossed around by his superiors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered about' is the anagram signal for PRIVATE JOE.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a disparaging remark is a nasty, belittling one.

clue.text: Costs halved by new rulers

indicators.note: halved by says the word is split into two equal parts by the letter placed in its middle

parts.note: costs are prices

explanation.surface: A fresh government cuts expenses by fifty per cent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'halved by' removes nothing: the word for costs is split into two equal parts with the new letter between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sovereign heads of principalities are monarchs who govern.

clue.text: I am put out after concert's short musical piece

indicators.note: after says the rearranged word follows the concert

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
a prom is a promenade concert, like those held each summer at London's Albert Hall

indicators.note: out means out of order, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A listener is annoyed when the recital offers only a brief item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' reads as annoyed, but 'out' is an anagram signal making PTU, and 'after' places it behind the concert.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a brief composition written to sound improvised, such as Schubert's for piano.

clue.text: Characters in trams, i.e. conductors

indicators.note: the characters in the words are their letters, taken to be arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Colourful people on the streetcars, namely those selling the tickets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters in' is the anagram signal for TRAMS IE. The conductors lead orchestras rather than collect fares.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian plural for masters of music, a title given to those who direct orchestras.

clue.text: Make unsound interpretation of speech

parts.note: unsound means without sound here: understanding what someone says by sight alone, watching the mouth

explanation.surface: Someone badly misunderstands an address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsound' pretends to mean faulty; it means done without hearing anything.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow talk by watching the mouth is to understand it with no hearing involved.

clue.text: Inanimate face showing no emotion

parts.note: something inanimate is dead, without life
pan is slang for the face

explanation.surface: A lifeless expression gives nothing away.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an expressionless delivery, as of a comic keeping a straight look.

clue.text: Expression, of approval curate only partly got

definitions.meaning: an old-fashioned British way of calling someone a thoroughly decent sort
in the 1895 Punch cartoon a curate served a bad breakfast item insists that parts of it are excellent

explanation.definitionFit: It is a hearty compliment for a decent person, and what the cartoon clergyman had only in parts.

clue.text: Italian known for writing plays, or performing one

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
an actor who is on is performing on stage
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A dramatist from Italy who might also act in his own work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' looks like a link word but is the heraldic term for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Carlo of that name was the 18th-century Venetian dramatist who wrote The Servant of Two Masters.

clue.text: Where convict returns, having pinched ring?

definitions.text: Where convict returns, having pinched ring?

indicators.note: to pinch is to grab and hold, so the word takes the letter inside
returns says the word for the convict is read coming back the other way

parts.note: lag is slang for a convict, as in old lag
a ring is the round letter O

explanation.surface: A jewel thief ends up back where he came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' makes LAG into GAL and 'having pinched' puts O inside; the whole clue also describes the place.
explanation.definitionFit: The British spelling of jail: a thief caught stealing jewellery is sent back to prison.

clue.text: Cleaner hasn't finished in Irish house

indicators.note: hasn't finished says the word stops short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a daily is British for a domestic cleaner who comes in each day

explanation.surface: The char has not yet done her work in a home in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't finished' drops the Y of DAILY. The house is a chamber of parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the lower chamber of the parliament of Ireland in Dublin.

clue.text: Dramatic part highly valued by player

definitions.note: read as a noun phrase: a thing a musician prizes greatly

indicators.note: part says only some consecutive letters of the word before it are used

explanation.surface: A stage role that an actor treasures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' takes letters from inside Dramatic. The player is a violinist, not an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Violins from this Cremona family of makers are instruments musicians treasure and pay fortunes for.

clue.text: A substance to feed animals

parts.note: the gist of an argument is its substance

explanation.surface: Some material for giving to livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal and farming verb: to take in another's livestock and pasture them for payment.

clue.text: One' positive response can produce more

definitions.note: more of the same: several affirmative replies, a plural noun

parts.note: one of something is 'a'
yes is an affirmative reply

explanation.surface: A single encouraging reply tends to bring others.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the wordplay: 'more' means more positive responses.
explanation.definitionFit: Votes in favour are several affirmative replies, the plural the clue's last word points back to.

clue.text: Girl without work is retiring

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so the timid word goes round the other

parts.note: a retiring person is shy
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A young woman with no job is giving up her career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' has its old sense of outside, as in 'without the city walls'. 'retiring' is about temperament, not pensions.
explanation.definitionFit: A diminutive of Sophia, so an example of a female name.

clue.text: Chairman I put on record — his views are one-sided

definitions.note: read as a noun: someone whose views are one-sided

indicators.note: put on says these pieces are added in front of the last one

parts.note: a professor, prof for short, holds a university chair
to record items is to list them

explanation.surface: The committee head and I go into the minutes, though he is thoroughly biased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' joins the pieces in order. 'one-sided' is literal: a side-on portrait, not a biased opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: This artist draws faces in outline seen side-on, so each picture shows one half of the head.

clue.text: Kept out of post, one intellectual appears hard-headed

parts.note: a letter kept out of the post is unsent
I is the Roman numeral one
mental means of the intellect

explanation.surface: Denied a job, a certain academic seems tough-minded about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The post is the mail, not a job, and 'intellectual' is an adjective rather than a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: practical and unmoved by feeling.
